walk_forward_validation_summary.evaluation_protocol: Strict Expanding-Window Walk-Forward Validation (train on all historical rounds strictly prior to target race)

evaluated_seasons_breakdown.2024: Rounds 1 to 24 (24 races, trained expanding from 67 prior rounds)
evaluated_seasons_breakdown.2026: Rounds 1 to 18 (18 races, up to Singapore GP; Round 19 Mexico held out as out-of-sample test)

delta_mae_vs_grid.true_meaning: Mean Absolute Error reduction (in finishing positions) of RidgeRank (3.0359) compared to the Starting Grid baseline (3.1299) across 66 walk-forward races. Negative means lower error (better accuracy). It is NOT positions gained by a driver.

spearman_rank_correlation_overall.calculation_method: Arithmetic mean of the 66 individual intra-race Spearman rank correlation coefficients (scipy.stats.spearmanr) across 2024-2026 walk-forward races

spearman_rank_correlation_mexico_2026.calculation_method: Single-race Spearman rank correlation between actual FinishPosition and pred_ridge_rank across all 22 drivers in 2026 Round 19 (Mexico City GP)

top_3_podium_hit_rate.mexico_2026_out_of_sample_podium_hit_rat: 2/3 (66.7% in Top 3: ['HAM', 'VER']; 3/3 [100.0%] of actual podium captured in Top 5)
top_3_podium_hit_rate.calculation_method: For each of the 66 walk-forward races, take the top 3 drivers with lowest pred_ridge_cont (ranks 1, 2, 3) and count how many actually finished in P1, P2, or P3 (order-agnostic set intersection divided by 3). Identical for pred_ridge_rank, p_podium_lr, and grid_pos (137/198 = 69.1919%).

feature_importance_verification.preprocessing: sklearn.preprocessing.StandardScaler (zero mean, unit variance per feature across training rows)
feature_importance_verification.coefficient_interpretation: Standardized regression weight (beta_j): expected change in predicted finishing position (1..22) per +1.0 standard deviation increase in feature X_j. Positive coefficient means a higher feature value (e.g. worse qualifying position number) increases predicted finishing position number (worse finish).
feature_importance_verification.note_on_reported_top4: The reported values (+2.06, +0.90, +0.88, +0.54) come from the 132-round pre-Mexico RidgeCV fit (+2.0666, +0.9069, +0.8875, +0.5466), truncated at 2 decimal places.

rolling_3_race_form_verification.formula: Simple unweighted mean of FinishPosition over the 3 immediately preceding races (Rounds 17, 18, 19 of 2026)

podium_probability_investigation.origin_of_40_2_pct: HistGradientBoostingClassifier (max_depth=3, min_samples_leaf=20, l2_regularization=1.0) trained on 2,676 historical rows (2021-2026 R19) and calibrated via log-odds shift so race podium probabilities sum to 3.0. It does NOT come from a Monte Carlo simulation.

why_hgb_disagrees_with_lr_and_ridge.summary: HistGradientBoostingClassifier exhibits non-monotonic tree-split overfitting on sparse tail combinations (elite driver_form_3 <= 1.67 paired with extreme back-grid start >= P19 and wet quali_gap_pct > 5%). Because monotonic constraints (monotonic_cst) were not enforced in HistGradientBoostingClassifier, its depth-3 decision trees learned an inverted split where having a worse grid_pos and worse quali_gap_pct actually INCREASES predicted podium probability for a driver with elite form.
why_hgb_disagrees_with_lr_and_ridge.key_proof_finding: When Verstappen's grid_pos is improved from P21 (z=+1.79) to the series average P10.5 (z=0.0), HGB's raw podium probability DROPS from 36.06% to 25.12%. When his quali_gap_pct is improved from +5.18% (z=+1.69) to average (z=0.0), HGB's raw podium probability DROPS from 36.06% to 22.85%. Conversely, setting driver_form_3 from 1.67 (z=-1.65) to average drops HGB raw probability from 36.06% to 1.64%. Thus, 40.2% is an unconstrained tree-split artifact, whereas LogisticRegression (0.61%) and RidgeCV (Expected Pos 12.01) preserve monotonic penalty scaling.

russia_2021_r15.note: Started P20 and finished P2, but his rolling 3-race form entering Russia 2021 was 6.67 (due to Silverstone & Monza crashes), NOT <= 2.0, so it was not in the elite-form leaf.

belgium_2022_r14.note: Won from Grid P13 (raw P14) with driver_form_3 = 1.33, but he qualified P1 fastest (quali_pos=1.0, quali_gap_pct=0.0%), unlike Brazil 2026 where he qualified P16 (+5.18% gap).

brazil_2024_r21.note: Won from Grid P15 (raw P17), but driver_form_3 was 3.67 and quali_pos was 10.0.

brazil_2025_r21.note: Closest actual match in the training set: Verstappen qualified P16, started P19 with driver_form_3 = 2.00, and finished P3.

audit_verdict_on_famous_recoveries_claim.empirical_base_rate_in_training_data: Across all 2,676 driver-starts (133 races), there are 8 instances of a driver starting Grid P14 or worse with driver_form_3 <= 2.5. Only 2 of 8 (25.0%) finished on the podium: 2025 R21 VER (Grid 19 -> P3) and 2026 R13 ANT (Grid 16 -> P1).
